title: The Essential Ingredient Of A Well-Behaved Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the true prerequisite for a well-behaved class isn't a specific technique but a teacher's belief that it's genuinely possible, since accepting the many reasons it 'can't be done' seals a teacher's fate before they even begin. He illustrates the point through the quiet, unassuming teacher on every campus who proves it can be done without fanfare, and through fleeting glimpses teachers sometimes catch of their own classes working perfectly, which should prompt real curiosity about what's different in those moments rather than dismissal as luck. He acknowledges that belief may come naturally to some (a stubborn refusal to accept limits) but insists the belief can also simply be chosen, even by teachers who have never experienced it and for whom it doesn't come naturally. The actionable claim is that deciding it's possible is the single biggest hurdle, and clearing it puts a teacher ahead of the vast majority of struggling peers, positioning them to acquire and apply the knowledge that turns belief into reality.
points: The single biggest determinant of classroom management success is a teacher's belief that it's actually achievable, not any specific technique.
Fleeting moments when a class 'just works' should prompt real investigation into what was different, rather than being dismissed as luck.
Belief doesn't have to come naturally -- teachers who've never experienced success can still choose to decide it's possible.
Deciding it's possible is described as jumping ahead of 99 percent of struggling teachers, positioning a teacher to act on real knowledge.
quotes: The essential ingredient of a well-behaved class is your belief that it’s possible.
Because as soon as you accept the myriad reasons why it can’t be done, which bombard teachers like West Texas hail, you’ve sealed your fate.
On nearly every campus there is at least one teacher quietly proving that it can be done. Without fanfare. Without bravado. Without any outward sign that they’re anything special.
It makes you wonder: Why does it work so perfectly every once in a while? What am I doing differently? How can I repeat these moments?
When you determine it’s possible, you’ve jumped the line in front of 99 percent of struggling teachers. You’ve overcome the biggest hurdle.
And thus, are now free to go and get it. To join the tens of thousands of teachers who’ve acquired the knowledge and can now create the well-behaved class they really want.
